Stewart, Calculus: Early Transcendentals · Section 15.8 · Exercise 26

Volume Cut from a Sphere by an Off-Centre Cylinder

Problem

Use cylindrical coordinates.

(a) Find the volume of the solid that the cylinder r=acosθ cuts out of the sphere of radius a centred at the origin.

(b) Illustrate the solid of part (a) by graphing the sphere and the cylinder on the same screen.

Reading the solid

The sphere has the equation x2+y2+z2=a2. The cylinder has the polar equation r=acosθ. Multiply by r to see what this circle is:

r=acosθ⟺r2=ar⟺x2+y2=ax⟺(x−2a​)2+y2=(2a​)2.

So the cylinder has radius a/2 and its axis is the vertical line through (a/2,0,0). The axis is off centre: it lies inside the sphere, so the solid is the part of the sphere that also lies inside the cylinder.

The solid is therefore

E={(r,θ,z):−2π​≤θ≤2π​, 0≤r≤acosθ, −a2−r2​≤z≤a2−r2​}.

The range −π/2≤θ≤π/2 is part of the description, not an extra assumption. The radius r is a distance, so r≥0, and r≤acosθ can hold only where cosθ≥0. The angle θ must stay in that half of the plane.

The two surfaces meet on a closed curve, the intersection of the sphere and the cylinder. On that curve x2+y2=ax, so the sphere gives ax+z2=a2, that is z=±a(a−x)​. The curve has two branches, one above and one below the xy-plane.

Look at the solid from above. Its shadow in the xy-plane is the disk that the cylinder cuts there, and that disk is the region r≤acosθ.

Setting up the integral

In cylindrical coordinates the volume element is dV=rdzdrdθ. The height of the solid above the point (r,θ) is the distance between the lower and upper sheets of the sphere:

2a2−r2​.

Insert this height and the limits of E:

V=∫−π/2π/2​∫0acosθ​∫−a2−r2​a2−r2​​rdzdrdθ=∫−π/2π/2​∫0acosθ​2ra2−r2​drdθ.

Evaluating the integral

Step 1. Integrate with respect to r. Put u=a2−r2, so du=−2rdr. Then

∫2ra2−r2​dr=−∫u1/2du=−32​u3/2=−32​(a2−r2)3/2.

At the upper limit r=acosθ,

a2−r2=a2−a2cos2θ=a2sin2θ,(a2sin2θ)3/2=a3∣sinθ∣3.

The absolute value is needed because the square root is a distance. So the integral over r gives the slice volume

∫0acosθ​2ra2−r2​dr=32​a3(1−∣sinθ∣3).

Step 2. Integrate with respect to θ. The slice depends on ∣sinθ∣, and the two halves of the interval give equal values. Double the integral over 0≤θ≤π/2, where sinθ≥0 and the absolute value can be dropped:

V=2∫0π/2​32​a3(1−sin3θ)dθ=34​a3∫0π/2​(1−sin3θ)dθ.

Reduce sin3θ with sin2θ=1−cos2θ and the substitution u=cosθ:

∫0π/2​sin3θdθ=∫0π/2​(1−cos2θ)sinθdθ=[−cosθ+3cos3θ​]0π/2​=1−31​=32​.

Hence

V=34​a3(2π​−32​)=32​a3(π−34​)=92a3(3π−4)​.

Checking the value

The answer must lie between two known volumes. The sphere holds 4πa3/3, and the cylinder holds π(a/2)2(2a)=πa3/2. The solid is the overlap of the two, so its volume must not exceed the smaller value:

92a3(3π−4)​≈1.2055a3<2πa3​≈1.5708a3<34πa3​≈4.1888a3.

The overlap is about three quarters of the cylinder, namely 1.2055/1.5708=0.767 of it, as it should be, because the cylinder lies well inside the sphere. As a fraction of the sphere the volume is

4πa3/3V​=2ππ−4/3​=21​−3π2​≈0.2878.

Three independent computations give the same number for a=1, namely 1.205506. They are the closed form, a double quadrature, and a Monte Carlo count of points that lie in both solids.

Answer

(a) The volume is

V=∫−π/2π/2​∫0acosθ​∫−a2−r2​a2−r2​​rdzdrdθ=92a3(3π−4)​=32​a3(π−34​)≈1.2055a3.

(b) The solid is drawn by plotting the sphere and the cylinder on the same axes. The sphere is x2+y2+z2=a2 and the cylinder is (x−a/2)2+y2=(a/2)2. The part of the sphere inside the cylinder is the solid of part (a).

Notation

SymbolMeaning
cylindrical coordinatesThe triple (r,θ,z), where r is the distance from the z-axis, θ is the angle from the positive x-axis, and z is the usual height. The volume element is dV=rdzdrdθ.
r=acosθA circle through the origin with centre (a/2,0) and radius a/2. In Cartesian form it is x2+y2=ax.
−π/2≤θ≤π/2The set of angles where cosθ≥0. Outside this range the bound r≤acosθ would give a negative radius, which is impossible.
∣sinθ∣The height factor at the wall of the cylinder. It is positive on the right half of the base and negative on the left half, and the slice volume uses its absolute value.
intersection curveThe set of points on both surfaces, z=±a(a−x)​. It is also called a Viviani curve. The two branches are the upper and lower rims of the solid.
overlapThe solid is the intersection of the ball x2+y2+z2≤a2 and the solid cylinder (x−a/2)2+y2≤(a/2)2.

Verification

  • part1_step1.py derives the volume symbolically and prints each stage: the vertical extent 2a∣sinθ∣, the antiderivative, the slice volume, the wall value ∫0π/2​sin3θdθ=2/3, and the result. It also confirms that the result equals 32​a3(π−34​) and evaluates it for a=1 and a=2.
  • part1_step2.py fixes a=1 and compares three values: the closed form 1.205506, double quadrature 1.20550621, and a Monte Carlo count 1.204771 with six million samples.
  • part1_figure1.py draws the sphere, the cylinder, and the two branches of the intersection curve. part1_figure2.py draws the base region.
